title: India's Private Banks Face Margin Squeeze as Retail Lending Slows
excerpt: HDFC Bank led a sell-off in private lenders after reporting weaker-than-expected net interest margins for the June quarter, while ICICI Bank emerged as the sector's standout performer.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • HDFC Bank's net interest margin fell to 3.26%, causing a 5.1% drop in share price.
  • ICICI Bank reported a 16% profit rise, earning an upgrade to 'outperform' from Bernstein.
  • Axis Bank's NIM of 3.46% is considered the 'cycle bottom' amid declining margins.
  • Corporate lending growth is strong, but retail lending is slowing, impacting profitability.
  • HDFC Bank's net interest margin fell to 3.26%, well below the 4% level it maintained before its 2023 merger, triggering a 5.1% share price decline.
  • ICICI Bank was the standout performer, reporting a 16% profit rise to ₹14,805 crore and earning an upgrade to "outperform" from Bernstein.
  • Axis Bank called its NIM of 3.46% the "cycle bottom," while Kotak Mahindra Bank hit its lowest margin in nearly five years at 4.53%.
  • Loan growth across major private lenders remained healthy at 15–20%, but a shift toward lower-margin corporate credit is compressing profitability.

India's largest private banks reported strong loan growth for the June quarter but saw profitability come under pressure as lending margins contracted across the board, raising questions about whether the sector's earnings trajectory can hold.

Shares of HDFC Bank, the country's largest private lender by assets, fell 5.1% on Monday — their steepest single-day drop in four months — after the bank posted a net interest margin (NIM) of 3.26% for Q1 FY27. The reading was unchanged sequentially but remained well below the 4% level HDFC Bank commanded before its 2023 merger with parent HDFC Ltd.

Margins Under Pressure Across the Board

All four top private lenders — HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank — reported their June quarter results over the weekend, and the theme was consistent: strong credit growth paired with thinning margins.

The Reserve Bank of India's cumulative rate cuts have begun filtering into lending rates faster than into funding costs, squeezing the net interest income that banks earn on each rupee lent.

"While margins were expected to contract this quarter, those of HDFC and Axis disappointed as they dropped more than expected."

— Anand Dama, Executive Director and Head of BFSI, Nuvama Institutional Equities

HDFC Bank's pre-provision operating profit fell 21.2% year-on-year to ₹28,168 crore, even as standalone net profit rose 5% to ₹19,060 crore, supported by a sharp 79% decline in provisions. CEO Sashi Jagdishan struck an optimistic note, saying the bank was "on the verge of pressing the pedal" on advances and that deposit growth was tracking above historical Q1 trends.

Axis Bank reported a 23% jump in net profit to ₹7,114 crore but saw its NIM fall to 3.46%, down from 3.62% the previous quarter. Its management called the reading a "cycle bottom." Amitabh Chaudhry, the bank's CEO, said Axis would focus on deploying additional liquidity raised through FCNR(B) deposits.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's NIM slipped to 4.53% from 4.67% in the March quarter and 4.65% a year earlier, though its net profit climbed 26% to ₹4,123 crore on the back of lower credit costs and healthy fee income growth.

ICICI Bank Breaks From the Pack

ICICI Bank was the clear outlier. The lender reported profit after tax of ₹14,805 crore, up 16% year-on-year, with net interest income rising 12.7% to ₹24,384 crore and core operating profit climbing 15.6%.

Bernstein upgraded ICICI Bank to "outperform" from "neutral" after the results, while Investec moved in the opposite direction on HDFC Bank, downgrading it to "hold" from "buy."

"At ICICI Bank, our strategic focus continues to be on growing profit before tax, excluding treasury, through the 360-degree customer-centric approach."

— Sandeep Bakhshi, MD and CEO, ICICI Bank

Corporate Lending Grows, Retail Slows

Across the sector, corporate lending accelerated while retail loan growth decelerated — a mix that naturally compresses margins since wholesale credit carries thinner spreads.

HDFC Bank's corporate and wholesale loans grew 18.6% year-on-year, while its retail book expanded just 7.2%. Axis Bank's wholesale banking book surged 38%, compared with 8% growth in retail advances. Loan growth among the major private lenders remained in the 15–20% range during the quarter, according to Jefferies.

The private bank index fell 2.3% on Monday, while the broader Nifty 50 dipped 0.4%. HDFC Bank extended losses into Tuesday, hitting a five-week low with a further 2.1% decline.

What It Means for Depositors and Investors

For depositors, the rate-cutting cycle should gradually bring down fixed-deposit rates, though banks are competing aggressively for stable funding. HDFC Bank's CASA ratio slipped to 32.3% from 32.8% a year earlier, while Axis Bank's term deposits grew 21%.

Asset quality remained a bright spot. HDFC Bank's gross NPAs improved to 1.17% from 1.40% a year earlier. ICICI Bank's GNPA stood at 1.67%, while Axis Bank's fell to 1.28% from 1.54%.

Analysts will be watching whether the margin trough has arrived — as Axis Bank's management suggested — or whether further rate cuts will continue to erode profitability through FY27.
